data.gender_notes: Nimisha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Nimisha is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Nimisha’, which means 'impression', 'mark', or 'sign'. In Hindu mythology, Nimisha is the goddess of time and is often depicted as the wife of Lord Mahadev. She is believed to hold the cosmic time in her hands and is known for her compassionate nature. The name Nimisha carries the meaning “Impression, mark, sign” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Nimisha usually hope their child will grow to embody impression, mark, sign and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Nimisha holds deep cultural significance in Hinduism as it is the name of the goddess of time. In various Hindu texts, imagery and mythology, Nimisha is described as the giver of boons, the dispenser of time, and the guardian of the universe. Thus, the name Nimisha is often associated with the concept of time, transformation, and change.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Nimisha holds profound significance, representing the fleeting, transient nature of our material existence. It reminds us that all things, including our lives, are marked by time and subject to change. Nimisha is also considered the embodiment of compassion, for she is believed to be the one who decides the span of our earthly lives. Thus, the name Nimisha signifies the interconnectedness of all things, the impermanence of life, and the compassionate presence that pervades the cosmos.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nimisha, derived from the Sanskrit word 'Nimisha' meaning 'moment' or 'instant', symbolizes the transient nature of life and the importance of cherishing each moment. It embodies the spiritual belief in living fully in the present.
